panels.title: Fire Success Rate
panels.description:
Share of finished tasks that succeeded over the range.

When bad: below ~90% means handler failures — break it down by task type. One type points to a node bug, all types to infra/DB.

targets.query:
import "array"

every = if int(v: v.windowPeriod) > int(v: 1m) then v.windowPeriod else 1m

from(bucket: "${bucket}")
  |> range(start: v.timeRangeStart, stop: v.timeRangeStop)
  |> filter(fn: (r) => r._measurement == "n8n" and (r._field == "n8n_scheduler_tasks_completed_total"))
  |> filter(fn: (r) => contains(value: r["task_type"], set: ${task_type:json}))
  |> filter(fn: (r) => contains(value: r["url"], set: ${instance:json}))
  |> increase()
  |> last()
  |> group()
  |> reduce(
    identity: {ok: 0.0, total: 0.0},
    fn: (r, accumulator) => ({
      ok: accumulator.ok + (if r.result == "success" then r._value else 0.0),
      total: accumulator.total + r._value,
    }),
  )
  |> map(fn: (r) => ({"Fire Success Rate": if r.total > 0.0 then r.ok / r.total else 0.0}))

panels.title: Oldest Pending Age
panels.description:
Age of the oldest due task; 0 means no due backlog. Aggregated with max.

When bad: sustained growth means dispatch can't keep up — check DB load and main count, and use the Per-Main Breakdown row to isolate a node.

targets.query:
import "array"

every = if int(v: v.windowPeriod) > int(v: 1m) then v.windowPeriod else 1m

from(bucket: "${bucket}")
  |> range(start: v.timeRangeStart, stop: v.timeRangeStop)
  |> filter(fn: (r) => r._measurement == "n8n" and (r._field == "n8n_scheduler_oldest_pending_age_seconds"))
  |> filter(fn: (r) => contains(value: r["url"], set: ${instance:json}))
  |> aggregateWindow(every: every, fn: last, createEmpty: false)
  |> group(columns: ["_time"])
  |> max()
  |> group(columns: [])
  |> keep(columns: ["_time", "_value"])
  |> rename(columns: {_value: "Oldest Pending Age"})

panels.title: Dead-letters (range)
panels.description:
Tasks permanently failed after exhausting attempts, over the range.

When bad: any dead-letter is a permanently failed task — inspect that task type's logs and the Per-Main Breakdown row.

targets.query:
import "array"

every = if int(v: v.windowPeriod) > int(v: 1m) then v.windowPeriod else 1m

union(tables: [
  from(bucket: "${bucket}")
    |> range(start: v.timeRangeStart, stop: v.timeRangeStop)
    |> filter(fn: (r) => r._measurement == "n8n" and (r._field == "n8n_scheduler_tasks_dead_lettered_total"))
    |> filter(fn: (r) => contains(value: r["url"], set: ${instance:json}))
    |> increase()
    |> last()
    |> group()
    |> keep(columns: ["_value"]),
  array.from(rows: [{_value: 0.0}]),
])
  |> group()
  |> sum()
  |> rename(columns: {_value: "Dead-letters (range)"})

When bad: below ~90% means handler failures — break it down by task type. One type points to a node bug, all types to infra/DB.

panels.title: Dispatch Lag — p50 / p90 / p99
panels.description:
Delay from a task becoming due to being dispatched.

When bad: p99 diverging while p50 stays low means a subset of tasks is stuck (lease contention, DB locks) — compare by task type and by main.
